learning_objective: 🎯 Master the reverse of trigonometry! Learn how to find the original angle when you already know the trigonometric ratio.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If standard trigonometry takes an angle and gives you a number (like sin(30°) = 1/2), inverse trigonometry takes the number and gives you back the angle (like arcsin(1/2) = 30°).

Because trigonometric functions repeat infinitely, their inverses would give multiple answers. To fix this, mathematicians restricted the answers to a specific, unique range called the Principal Value Branch.
Just like standard algebra, inverse trig functions have special identities and formulas that let you simplify complex expressions and solve equations easily.

fun_activity.title: 📐 The Shadow Reversal
fun_activity.instructions: Measure the height of an object and the length of its shadow. Divide the height by the shadow length to get the tangent ratio. Now use the 'tan⁻¹' button on a calculator to find the exact angle of the sun in the sky!

exam_tips: 📌 ALWAYS check if your final answer lies within the Principal Value Branch. If it doesn't, use quadrant rules (like π - θ) to bring it inside.
📌 Memorize the domain and range table for all six inverse functions—it is a guaranteed 1-mark objective question.
📌 Be careful with negative values: sin⁻¹(-x) = -sin⁻¹(x), but cos⁻¹(-x) = π - cos⁻¹(x).
quick_recap: ⭐ Inverse trigonometric functions help us find unknown angles.
⭐ We must always restrict our answers to the principal value branch to keep it a valid function.
⭐ Watch out for the negative signs inside the inverse functions!
